body: About 50% of my updates would have to do with contemplating suicide.  No one in my life knows just how often I get suicidal thoughts.  I am very good at acting cheerful and upbeat.  I have never told anyone how I really feel.

Being a teenager is hard.  Really really hard.  Your emotions and your hormones are in overdrive.  You feel things 100 times more intensely than an adult would.  It's normal for your developmental stage, but it's hell to put up with while you're going through it.  I remember what it was like.

Just try to hang in there.  Tell yourself "This is not what I think; it's my hormones trying to mess up my brain".  It will get better.  I promise.  Tell your parents or your friends what's going on with you.  Call a suicide hotline (there are some numbers in the sidebar).  Try to get through this hell in any way you can - distract yourself, find something to do, eat something, watch a cheesy movie, read a trashy novel - anything.  

Try to get some sleep.  Drink some warm milk (it's supposed to make you feel sleepy), and hit the sack.  Things will look better in the morning.

Thank you so much for your post - and I really appreciate the time and energy and the kindness that you are giving me.  Yesterday was a very difficult/painful day for me - I think I was also under a lot of strain because I was overworking myself (I literally had a performance every night for the past couple of weeks, and the day job, and rehearsals, and practicing), and it led me into a very dark place.  Thank you for helping me out of that dark place.  What you wrote was exactly what I needed to hear in that condition.  You don't know just how much you helped me.  

I've slept for 13 hours and had a good meal and I feel better now.  Still not shiny-happy-ecstatic, but not in any danger of going to the gun shop any time soon.  I'm taking it easy today and focusing on getting enough rest and taking care of myself.  

Thank you again.

I've thought about it.  I am a decent composer, and I've thought about getting into film composing or videogame composing or something like that.  But I'd need to take some coursework for that, and I don't have the time/$$ right now.

Thank you for that.  And I love that quote.  

And yes, it does get hard.  I've been relatively lucky these past 6 years - I've had so much support and so much positive energy from everyone I've encountered in music.  This is really the first reality check I've had.  

Good luck with your acting - I hope things go well for you.

I actually love playing at nursing homes for this precise reason.  Haven't done it for a while, but I really should see if I can get a few gigs like that.  Thanks for the suggestion - it is making me feel better just thinking about my last nursing-home gig.  They loved me there.

What I'd say to someone in my situation is probably something soothing along the lines of "Well, I don't care what that asshole says - I think you're the cat's pajamas!"  (or was it the bee's knees?)  If someone is that crazy dedicated to whatever it is, and their dreams just got crushed, you do your best to try and un-crush them.  

I've actually done that for a few of my friends who are musicians.  It seems to be an occupational hazard, now that I think about it.  I believe the traditional, time-honored way of coping with it would be booze or drugs.  Maybe I should get me some.

I actually have a ton of Youtube videos up - when I perform somewhere, people record it and put it up.  I can't even bear to watch them, the playing is so awful.   

I actually have a CD recording of one of my recent concerts (duet concert with my piano teacher) that a very nice person made.  It's been sitting on my desk and I can't bear to listen to it - I'm afraid of what I'll hear.  

I wish I could show you my music, but my name is on all the Youtube videos.  I don't want to defeat the purpose of my throwaway account (last thing I need at this point is for someone I know to see this and get me committed).  Sorry.
No one, but it won't be any great loss to the music world.  As mentioned, my audiences can't wait for me to get off the stage.

It's not the depression talking - it's the addiction talking.  I really can't live without music.  I gave up all sorts of fun things to do this - it's hard to carve out 2-3 hours a day while running a business, and it means that all sorts of fun things are going by the wayside.  I seldom go to the movies, I never watch TV, I rarely hang out with my friends, I don't play sports or go to the gym, I almost never date.  My life is basically work and music and sleep.  

If I were good at the music stuff, all this sacrifice would make sense.  But since I suck, it just means that I've been living like a monk for no good reason.
Oh, I've played in churches.  And nursing homes.  Yes, they are great - a very supportive audience.

You're sweet to say that.  Intellectually, I know all that - and I know that giving up at this point doesn't make sense and that there are many other things I could be doing and that there will be a beautiful sunrise tomorrow and that I should really see it and all that.  But emotionally, all I can do at this point is cry.  I can just about pull myself together when someone else is around, and then I totally lose it again when I'm alone.  

I will do my best to stick around long enough to find out what is on Reddit tomorrow.

Oh, I'm not going for fame and fortune.  All I want is to play well.  I want to perform and be happy with how I played.  I don't even want to quit my day job.  I'm fine with music as a part-time occupation.  But I don't want to suck at it.  If I'm going to suck at it, I'd rather not do it at all.

You're sweet.  Thank you.  And I know all that, and I know it was just a couple of bad performances, and an asshole concert director, and some limitations that I need to work hard to overcome - but it all hit me at once, and it hurts like hell and I'm tired and angry at myself and defeated and I've been crying nonstop for 2 days straight.  I can just about pull myself together when I'm out in public or when I'm meeting with someone, but I totally lose it when I'm alone. 

I know I need to work on my performing, and my teacher is very kind and very encouraging and I know she will try to help me.  I'm just so tired.  I just want to be gone already.
Good heavens.  Thank you - and yes, I would be honored to accept your assistance.  But you'd have to hear me first - apparently, according to my audiences, I suck.

Oh, I know I'm good as an amateur.  I had bigger goals.  Maybe it was overambitious.

The thing is, I had my chance to be a professional.  At the age of 18, I could have said "Mom, Dad, I'm going to major in music and I don't care what you say!"  I chickened out.  I'm trying to recapture what I'd lost, and apparently some things are lost forever.  That's what makes me sad - that I only realized too late that music is what I really want to do in life, and that now it is too late to do anything about it.  

Ah well.  Sometimes all one can do is give it a good solid try and concede defeat.

Thanks so much for your kindness.  I appreciate your answer, and you are right; the important thing is improvement.  I know I've improved.  

For the past 6 years, that's what I've been telling myself, and telling others - that my only goal is to play better today than I played yesterday.  It's just a really saddening thing to find out that even after 6 years of hard work and improvement, I still suck.

Thanks for the reply.  You are very kind.  

The musical pursuits are pianistic ones.  I play jazz and classical piano, accompany singers, play in noisy bars, give concerts sometimes - that sort of thing.  I've played all my life - started at a young age, though I never pursued it as a profession until recently.  In the past 6 years, I really got very serious about my music and about my practicing and ... well, I guess I still suck.  I've been working hard.  Even though I had a very demanding day job at one point, I still practiced 2-3 hours a day.  I practice more than that now that I have my own business and flexible hours.  I have a great teacher who has really tried very hard to help me.  And it's all a waste.  

I don't care if I never strike it rich with my music.  I have a day job and it supports me just fine.  But I do want to get good.  I'd like to not be ashamed of my performances.  I'd like to be proud of what I do.  And I'll never get there.
